Mass Displacement · 1967-06-05 · Six-Day War (Israel vs Egypt, Jordan, Syria)

Summary

The Six-Day War erupted on June 5, 1967 when Israel launched preemptive strikes on Egyptian airfields, followed by ground operations. Within six days, Israel occupied the Egyptian-controlled Gaza Strip and Sinai Peninsula, Jordanian-controlled West Bank and East Jerusalem, and Syrian Golan Heights. The rapid Israeli victory fundamentally transformed the Israeli-Palestinian conflict by bringing all of historic Palestine under Israeli control.

Mass displacement began immediately. As Israeli forces advanced into the West Bank, panic spread among Palestinians remembering the 1948 Nakba. Estimates of those who fled or were expelled range from 280,000 (Israeli sources) to 400,000+ (Palestinian and UN sources). Approximately 175,000 were refugees from 1948 being displaced a second time. The displacement was not solely a byproduct of combat—Israeli authorities issued military orders preventing return and systematically demolished entire villages.

Three villages in the Latrun area (Imwas, Yalo, and Beit Nuba) were completely destroyed by Israeli forces, their 10,000 residents expelled. In Jerusalem's Old City, the Moroccan Quarter was bulldozed days after occupation to create a plaza at the Western Wall. UN Security Council Resolution 242 called for 'withdrawal of Israeli armed forces from territories occupied' and for 'achieving a just settlement of the refugee problem,' but Israel has maintained occupation for over 55 years. The 1967 displacement and subsequent occupation created the framework for the current Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

Timeline

1967-06-05 07:45:00 War begins - Operation FocusIsrael launches preemptive airstrikes destroying Egyptian air force on ground. Jordan and Syria enter war supporting Egypt. Israeli ground forces enter Sinai and Gaza. — UN Security Council Records 1967
5-6 June West Bank invasion; displacement beginsIsraeli forces cross into Jordanian West Bank. Mass exodus begins as Palestinians flee advancing Israeli army, fearing repeat of 1948. Israeli Radio broadcasts in Arabic encouraging Palestinians to flee. — Tom Segev - '1967: Israel, the War, and the Year that Transformed the Middle East'
2026-06-07 00:00:00 East Jerusalem occupiedIsraeli paratroopers capture Old City of Jerusalem. Defense Minister Moshe Dayan proclaims: 'We have returned to the holiest of our holy places, never to part from it again.' — UN Security Council Records
7-8 June Latrun villages demolishedVillages of Imwas, Yalo, and Beit Nuba in Latrun area ordered evacuated. Residents given hours to leave. IDF systematically demolishes all structures with bulldozers and explosives. ~10,000 residents expelled; prevented from return. — Zochrot Documentation
10-11 June Moroccan Quarter demolishedIsraeli authorities bulldoze Moroccan Quarter (Harat al-Maghariba) adjacent to Western Wall in Jerusalem's Old City. 135 houses destroyed, 650 residents expelled with minimal notice to create Western Wall plaza. — Wikipedia - Moroccan Quarter
2026-06-10 00:00:00 Ceasefire; occupation completeWar ends after six days. Israel occupies West Bank, Gaza, East Jerusalem, Golan Heights, Sinai Peninsula. Occupation of Palestinian territories continues to present day. — UN Security Council Resolutions
June-August 1967 Military orders prevent returnIsraeli military government issues orders preventing displaced Palestinians from returning. Identity card system established; those who left denied reentry. Property declared 'absentee property' subject to confiscation. — B'Tselem - Israeli Occupation Documentation
1967-06-14 00:00:00 UN General Assembly Emergency SessionEmergency session convened. Multiple resolutions condemn Israeli annexation of Jerusalem and call for allowing refugee return. Israel rejects all resolutions. — UN General Assembly Records

Testimony

Moshe DayanAfter capturing Old City, proclaimed: 'We have returned to the holiest of our holy places, never to part from it again.' Later reflected on displacement: 'We came to this country which was already populated by Arabs, and we are establishing...a Jewish state here.' Regarding Latrun villages: 'We had to destroy three Arab villages in the Latrun area.' — Various interviews and memoirs; Haaretz 1969
Amos ElonWitnessed destruction of Imwas village June 1967: 'Military bulldozers were finishing their work...not a stone was left standing...the wells were capped with concrete.' Described residents 'trudging down the main highway to Ramallah' with belongings. — Haaretz, June 1967; later compiled in 'The Israelis' (1971)
Hussein Musa (Imwas resident)Resident of Imwas village: 'The Israeli soldiers came and told us we had three hours to leave...we took what we could carry. When we looked back from the hills, they were destroying everything with bulldozers—our homes, our mosque, our cemetery. Everything.' — Oral history - Palestinian refugee documentation
Tom SegevIn '1967: Israel, the War, and the Year that Transformed the Middle East': 'Immediately after the war, Israel implemented measures that made refugees' return impossible.' Documented military orders preventing return, identity card confiscations. 'The government's position was that most of the refugees should not be allowed to return.' — 1967: Israel, the War, and the Year that Transformed the Middle East' (2007)
UN Secretary-General U ThantReport to Security Council: 'The displacement of the civilian population as a result of the conflict continues to cause great human suffering and poses a serious threat to peace and security.' Called for allowing refugees to return or receive compensation. — Report to UN Security Council, September 1967
International Committee of the Red CrossICRC stated Fourth Geneva Convention applicable to occupied territories. Documented mass displacement, house demolitions, prevention of return. Called on Israel to allow refugees to return and respect civilian protections under international humanitarian law. — ICRC statements and reports, 1967-1968

War crimes

Systematic Village DestructionThree entire villages (Imwas, Yalo, Beit Nuba) demolished within days of occupation. Residents given 1-3 hours to evacuate. All homes, mosques, churches, cemeteries systematically destroyed. Total 10,000 residents expelled; area converted to Canada Park. No compensation paid. — Zochrot Documentation
Moroccan Quarter DemolitionHistoric 770-year-old Jerusalem neighborhood bulldozed 48 hours after occupation. 135 houses, two mosques, zawiya (Islamic school) destroyed. 650 residents given 3 hours to evacuate. Afdal Mosque (12th century) and other heritage sites demolished. — Historical Documentation
Prevention of ReturnMilitary orders and identity card system prevented displaced Palestinians from returning home—direct violation of international humanitarian law. Fourth Geneva Convention Article 49: occupying power may not forcibly transfer or deport protected persons. — B'Tselem Documentation
Illegal AnnexationEast Jerusalem formally annexed June 28, 1967 (not recognized internationally). Golan Heights annexed 1981. UN Security Council declared annexations 'null and void.' Transfer of Israeli civilians into occupied territories violates Geneva Convention Article 49. — UN Resolutions
Mass Displacement300,000-400,000 Palestinians displaced during and immediately after war. Many forced out through psychological warfare (radio broadcasts), prevention of return, house demolitions. Approximately half were second-time refugees (displaced from 1948). — UNRWA Reports
Extrajudicial KillingsMultiple documented cases of POW killings and civilian deaths. Egyptian POWs killed at al-Arish. Systematic documentation prevented by denial of ICRC access during conflict. — ICRC Reports

Legal classification

Fourth Geneva Convention (1949) - ViolationsArticle 49: 'Individual or mass forcible transfers...of protected persons from occupied territory...are prohibited regardless of their motive.' Displacement and prevention of return violate this core protection.
UN Security Council ResolutionsResolution 242 (1967): Called for 'withdrawal of Israeli armed forces from territories occupied' and 'just settlement of refugee problem.' Remains foundation of peace process but unimplemented.
International Court of Justice Advisory Opinion (2004)Wall Advisory Opinion: ICJ ruled Israeli construction of separation barrier in West Bank illegal. Reaffirmed Fourth Geneva Convention applies to occupied Palestinian territories.
Ongoing Occupation - Modern AssessmentProlonged occupation: At 55+ years, Israeli occupation is longest military occupation in modern history. International law views prolonged occupation as raising additional legal concerns.
Fourth Geneva Convention (1949) - ViolationsArticle 49(6): 'The Occupying Power shall not deport or transfer parts of its own civilian population into the territory it occupies.' Israeli settlement enterprise violates this provision (over 700,000 settlers as of 2024).
UN Security Council ResolutionsResolution 252 (1968): Declared Israeli annexation measures in Jerusalem 'invalid.' Called on Israel to rescind all actions to change status of city.
International Court of Justice Advisory Opinion (2004)Settlements: ICJ confirmed Israeli settlements violate Article 49(6) of Geneva Convention. Called on Israel to cease settlement activity and dismantle existing settlements.
Ongoing Occupation - Modern AssessmentAnnexation de facto: While Israel never formally annexed West Bank, settlement enterprise and administrative integration constitute de facto annexation in violation of international law.
Fourth Geneva Convention (1949) - ViolationsArticle 53: 'Any destruction by the Occupying Power of...property...is prohibited, except where such destruction is rendered absolutely necessary by military operations.' Demolition of Latrun villages and Moroccan Quarter lacked military necessity.
UN Security Council ResolutionsResolution 298 (1971): Deplored Israeli failure to comply with previous resolutions regarding Jerusalem.
International Court of Justice Advisory Opinion (2004)Occupation obligations: ICJ held Israel bound by international humanitarian law and human rights law in occupied territories.
Ongoing Occupation - Modern AssessmentPopulation transfer: Transfer of over 700,000 Israeli civilians into occupied territory constitutes systematic violation of Geneva Convention Article 49(6).
Fourth Geneva Convention (1949) - ViolationsArticle 147 (Grave Breaches): Extensive destruction of property not justified by military necessity constitutes grave breach (war crime).
UN Security Council ResolutionsResolution 465 (1980): Determined that Israeli settlements in occupied territories 'have no legal validity' and constitute 'flagrant violation' of Geneva Convention.
UN Security Council ResolutionsResolution 478 (1980): Declared Israel's 'Basic Law' declaring Jerusalem its 'eternal capital' null and void.

Commanders

1915-1981 Moshe DayanLed Israeli military operations during Six-Day War. Made key decisions regarding occupation policies, including demolition of Latrun villages and Moroccan Quarter. Later expressed mixed feelings about occupation's long-term consequences.
1922-1995 Yitzhak RabinMilitary commander during Six-Day War. Oversaw operations in West Bank, East Jerusalem. Later as Prime Minister (1974-77, 1992-95) pursued peace negotiations; assassinated by Israeli extremist in 1995.
1895-1969 Levi EshkolIsraeli Prime Minister during Six-Day War. Made political decisions regarding occupation and settlement policies. Initially reluctant to occupy West Bank but approved military plans.
